metadata.date: ISO dates at the precision given by the source. For forecasts, date is the target period. For missing rows, date is the research cutoff.
metadata.confidence: measured = direct count from a named inventory or disclosed measurement; vendor-claim = company or industry disclosure, including attributed disclosures via press; estimate = model, analyst estimate or forecast. Missing rows have null confidence and source_url may identify a source checked.
metadata.qualifier: gt = strictly above the value; gte = at least the value; approx = rounded estimate; null = use the reported value as shown.
metadata.geography: Country codes follow ISO 3166-1 alpha-2. CN refers to mainland China. Market availability refers to a local line, with no roaming inference.
metadata.comparability: Group by metric, unit, geography and kind before charting. The monthly-user observations have different definitions. Do not connect them as a single time series. Forecasts belong in separate series.

timeline.note: Google starts broad US rollout after enabling chat features in the UK, France and Mexico.
Google declares global Android rollout through carriers or Google itself, subject to device and provider eligibility. One-to-one encryption enters beta.
GSMA Intelligence publishes an addressability model for operator and Google paths.
Google announces end-to-end encryption for eligible one-to-one Google Messages chats.
Juniper publishes a forecast for RCS-capable subscribers through 2026.
Vodafone announces Google Messages as the default on applicable Android devices and plans a Jibe Cloud migration.
Google Messages enables RCS by default for eligible users who have not switched it off and extends end-to-end encryption to eligible Google Messages group chats.
Google reports its monthly-active Google Messages milestone with RCS enabled.
Apple adds personal RCS to Messages with iOS 18 where carriers support it.
Apple adds carrier-dependent RCS Business Messaging in iOS 18.1.
GSMA announces Universal Profile 3.0 specifications, including interoperable encryption based on Messaging Layer Security.
KDDI launches iPhone RCS for au, UQ mobile and povo1.0.
Google publishes a daily RCS message-volume milestone.
GSMA announces Universal Profile 3.1 with audio messaging and onboarding updates.
LG U+, KT and SK Telecom add iPhone RCS with iOS 26.
GSMA announces Universal Profile 4.0, including richer text, media and a path to video calls. These are specification capabilities.
Apple and Google begin a default-on cross-platform encryption beta for eligible iOS 26.5 and Google Messages users.
US Samsung Messages end of service takes effect for Galaxy devices running Android 12 or newer.
GSMA publishes Universal Profile 4.1 with encryption interoperability refinements.
NTT DOCOMO starts native carrier RCS service and gradually replaces Jibe as the Android provider. Its iPhone path requires iOS 27.
Apple documents inline replies and Tapbacks in iOS 27 RCS.
Telstra starts carrier RCS rollout on compatible devices.

platform_features.note: Service can be Google-hosted or carrier-provided. Eligibility depends on device, region and service provider.
RCS defaults on for eligible Google Messages users unless previously disabled. This setting is independent of which app is the default texting app.
Samsung’s end-of-service notice is US-only. Android 11 and older are exempt. South Korea’s carrier Galaxy service has separate evidence.
Native personal RCS on an eligible carrier plan. Supports richer media and groups. Minimum version can be higher on individual carriers.
Apple documents selection of a default texting app for SMS, MMS and RCS, and a separate RCS Business Messages setting. Business messaging first appeared in iOS 18.1.

Messaging Layer Security-based interoperable encryption rollout began in beta, on by default for eligible chats. Requires a supporting iPhone carrier and a current Google Messages app. A lock indicates encryption for that conversation.
Apple documents Tapbacks and inline replies over RCS, plus end-to-end encryption when both ends support it.
